subject: Kickoff: Streaming + Tool Calling + Structured Output examples refresh (SDKs + docs)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Kickoff: Streaming + Tool Calling + Structured Output examples refresh (SDKs + docs)

Team —

Kicking off the “examples refresh” work for streaming + tool calling + structured output/JSON schema across SDKs + docs.

Why now: we’ve got inconsistent snippets across Python/TS/Go + docs pages, and support is seeing the same confusion patterns (stream assembly, partial tool args, JSON parse failures). We need a single canonical pattern that’s copy/paste runnable and versioned.

High-level goals:
- One consistent mental model for streaming across languages (event types, partial deltas, final message assembly, error branches)
- Tool calling examples aligned to what we actually support (tool defs, arg validation, parallel tool calls, tool-result messages)
- Structured output examples that show JSON schema constraints + safe parsing/validation + fallback/retry guidance

Proposed plan + tickets are in Linear (project):
https://linear.app/redwood/team/ENG/project/streaming-tool-calling-structured-output-examples-refresh-5f3c2a

Timeline: 4–6 weeks. Week 1 audit + parity matrix; Week 2 standards/spec; Weeks 2–4 implementation + tests; Weeks 4–6 review + publish.

Owners (proposed):
- SDK work: Monica (overall), with Ibrahim as parity TL; Dana (TS), Mateusz (Go)
- Docs updates: Elliot (overall), Wei on hosted API pages
- Product semantics/terminology: Nikhil + Henry
- I’ll sponsor/clear blockers and make sure we don’t “accidentally” design a new protocol

Asks for today:
1) Confirm scope + owners
2) Any “must-have” constraints for public messaging (Nikhil)
3) Any constraints for docs migration/redirects (Elliot)

If you’re aligned, I’ll have Talia put a weekly 20-min check-in on the calendar + we’ll treat the Linear project as source of truth.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex Martinez
VP, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Streaming + Tool Calling + Structured Output examples refresh (SDKs + docs)

Aligned on scope + owners.

A couple constraints / notes from SDK side:
- Examples must not rely on unreleased APIs. If we need tiny ergonomic helpers (e.g., assembling streaming deltas / tool-call args), we can do that as “examples utilities” with tests, but I don’t want to back ourselves into a breaking SDK change.
- Streaming: we should explicitly show how to handle partial tool-call arguments in the stream (accumulate string, parse only when we see “done”/final tool call) — this is the #1 footgun in Python and Go.
- Testing: I want “golden transcript” fixtures per language to keep event shapes stable. Otherwise we’ll drift again in 2 months.

I’ll sync with Ibrahim today and get an audit pass started (ENG-4821) + outline the parity matrix format.

Monica

Monica Patel
Director, SDK Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 10:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Streaming + Tool Calling + Structured Output examples refresh (SDKs + docs)

+1.

Docs constraints:
- We need to be very explicit about SDK version assumptions on every page (and ideally link to the released changelog tags once Connor cuts them). “Copy/paste works” includes “installs the right version.”
- We have a couple page renames/redirects in mind for the streaming + tool calling guide (the current taxonomy is confusing). Wei and I can draft migration notes; we’ll just need a clear “ship date” so we can coordinate redirects and search indexing.
- Please keep the canonical patterns consistent with the code tabs: same conceptual flow, same ordering, minimal language-specific embellishments.

If you’re good with it, I’ll have Kira start the internal “DX standards” Confluence pages in parallel (event naming, assembly rules, what to show vs hide in snippets).

Elliot

Elliot Price
Director, Technical Documentation
Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 11:22 AM PST
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Streaming + Tool Calling + Structured Output examples refresh (SDKs + docs)

Aligned.

Messaging constraints from Product:
- Please avoid implying “hard guarantees” for structured output across all models. We should document it as “schema-constrained / structured output support varies by model” and include a support matrix callout (Henry is already tracking PM-413).
- Tool calling: we need to stick to Redwood-supported semantics and be careful around OpenAI-compat differences. If examples mirror OpenAI payload shapes too closely, support gets dragged into “why does this field look different?” conversations.
- For streaming, please include a short note on disconnect/retry behavior (what is safe to retry vs what can duplicate tokens / tool calls).

Henry + I can review the public guides once the canonical pattern is drafted. Just tag PM-412/PM-413 and we’ll turn around comments quickly.

Nikhil

Nikhil Sharma
Director of Product, Hosted API
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 12:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Streaming + Tool Calling + Structured Output examples refresh (SDKs + docs)

Thanks — aligned on all points.

Summary / decisions:
- Scope confirmed: streaming + tool calling + structured output examples across Python/TS/Go SDKs + docs + runnable examples/quickstarts.
- Owners confirmed:
  - SDK: Monica (Ibrahim parity lead; Dana TS; Mateusz Go)
  - Docs: Elliot (Wei pages; Kira internal standards)
  - Product messaging + support matrix: Nikhil/Henry
- Constraints:
  - No unreleased APIs in examples; keep helpers lightweight and example-scoped
  - Golden transcript fixtures to prevent drift
  - Public language must avoid over-promising structured output guarantees; include model support matrix + OpenAI-compat notes

Next steps:
1) Monica/Ibrahim: week-1 audit + parity matrix (ENG-4821). Please post the draft canonical event naming/stream assembly recommendation in the Linear project by EOW.
2) Elliot: draft docs migration/redirect plan + version callouts.
3) Nikhil/Henry: review terminology + structured output support language once the spec draft is in.

Source of truth: Linear project link below.
https://linear.app/redwood/team/ENG/project/streaming-tool-calling-structured-output-examples-refresh-5f3c2a

I’ll ask Talia to set a weekly 20-min checkpoint (Mon/Wed) and we’ll treat blockers as “same-day” issues.

Alex

Alex Martinez
VP, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference
